Stock Market News for April 1, 2026 758 news published. RSS Feed Google News Major M&A and corporate moves Keurig Dr Pepper (KDP) closed a landmark deal to acquire JDE Peet's and named Rafael Oliveira as CEO of the combined global coffee business—consolidating brands and supply chains in consumer staples. (transaction details) OneStream (OS) announced the completion of its acquisition by Hg for $6.4 billion, a large private-equity exit that removes a public software asset from the market and reshapes enterprise-software M&A comps. (deal note) Gilead Sciences (GILD) extended its tender offer to acquire Arcellx, signaling persistence to close a strategically important cell-therapy tuck-in that would expand Gilead’s oncology footprint; investors should watch revised timelines and any financing or regulatory updates. (tender extension) Deals, financing and capital markets Micron (MU) announced the expiration of cash tender offers for certain senior notes—an active liability-management move that trims interest costs and signals capital-allocation priorities. American Assets Trust (AAT) increased its revolving line of credit to $500 million and extended the maturity under its amended credit agreement, a liquidity boost that supports development pipelines and REIT flexibility. (credit agreement) Stitch Fix (SFIX) resumed its share repurchase program, returning to buybacks as a tool to support the stock and signal confidence in free-cash-flow leverage—watch repurchase pace and offset against inventory dynamics. UMH Properties (UMH) issued a first-quarter 2026 operations update—keep an eye on occupancy, rent-growth trends and any guidance shifts for residential REITs. (operations update) AI, cloud, cyber and enterprise moves IBM (IBM) expanded its FedRAMP portfolio with authorization for 11 software solutions, including watsonx, broadening government cloud opportunities and enterprise AI sales cycles. Sharon AI (SHAZ) signed a 5‑year, $1.25B AI cloud infrastructure deal, underscoring durable hyperscaler and enterprise spending on AI-native capacity. (announcement) Shutterstock (SSTK) launched a licensed-content integration with ChatGPT, another sign of platform monetization as AI tools embed licensed assets into enterprise workflows. (product launch) Regulatory openings and market access eToro (ETOR) said it now offers cryptoasset investing in New York, opening a major U.S. retail market and signaling continued regulatory thaw for crypto platforms. Legal, litigation and corporate actions Churchill Downs Incorporated (CHDN) celebrated a district-court victory in its suit against the Horseracing Integrity and Safety Authority; the ruling reduces a regulatory overhang and clarifies legal risk for racing operators. (statement) Big contracts, transport and infrastructure Target Hospitality (TH) secured a $550M+ multi-year contract with a top-five hyperscaler to support data-center development—strengthening its workforce-housing pipeline tied to cloud buildouts. (contract note) Intel will repurchase a 49% equity interest in its Ireland fab joint venture, reshaping capital commitments and control over a strategic European manufacturing footprint—watch foundry strategy implications. (details) Space, defense and advanced tech AeroVironment (AVAV) was selected to deliver ISR services to the U.S. Navy with its JUMP 20‑X and advanced payload integrations—another defense win validating unmanned payload commercialization. (award note) EV deliveries and China auto momentum Li Auto (LI) issued its March delivery update, keeping a close watch on demand and supply-chain resilience in China’s EV market. (details) XPeng (XPEV) and NIO (NIO) released March and Q1 delivery figures—data that will influence near-term sentiment on growth, inventory and promotional intensity among Chinese EV OEMs. (XPeng | NIO) Stellantis (STLA) reported U.S. first-quarter sales up 4% year-over-year, a modest but meaningful sign of recovery in light-vehicle demand.
